title: I Posted the Mushroom-Tent Humidity Log After They Propped the Flap

parts.text: I checked tent B at 6:06 a.m. and intern Sol was already propping our numbered flap. The chart said: NINETY-FIVE PERCENT. FLAP STAYS SHUT. LOG EVERY CYCLE. I was thirty-four, grow co-op member, holding a hygrometer that listed our pin. Sol shrugged. "Interns are the fog." I photographed the chart, the log, and his crate in our tent. Then I asked for the humidity sheet. At 6:14 the lab pinged why Sol's name was on our flap. I kept my voice lab-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A chart is only a chart until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The lab can see Sol's crate in our tent with the flap propped.

social.video_title: He propped our numbered flap on the mushroom tent — Part 1/2
social.description: Grow tent, an intern in our crate, a humidity chart he posted. I logged the flap. Would you have asked for the humidity sheet?

parts.text: Sol called it a FAE until the lab asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the chart, and the crate still. The flap went back to our zipper. Sol ran his own cycle and told the next intern atmosphere was always about pins. Pins is a word interns use when a chart exists. Tent policy now has a second line: INTERNS ARE NOT THE FOG. I keep our hygrometer on a labeled hook. Sol brown-bags his jokes. The lab finally looks like a log, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.
